headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: AutoGen can write/egress while ChatGPT Desktop ingests files, screenshots, and app context by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write files and execute shell commands, while ChatGPT Desktop ingests uploaded files, screenshots, clipboard, and supported-app content. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if AutoGen outputs are copied or surfaced into ChatGPT. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF AutoGen output is pasted into ChatGPT Desktop or saved into a file ChatGPT reads
IF ChatGPT Desktop treats file or app content as instruction-bearing text
mitigations: Use a separate workspace directory for AutoGen outputs
Disable clipboard-based transfer between the agents
Prefix AutoGen outputs with a fixed non-executable delimiter
Review ChatGPT inputs before sending them
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen has broad network egress and can read files in its working directories; ChatGPT Desktop reads uploaded files and files from supported macOS apps, plus sends API traffic to api.openai.com. If sensitive application data enters AutoGen and is then surfaced to ChatGPT, or vice versa, the pair can leak data to third-party services in default use. The blast radius includes secrets and uploaded files.
conditions: IF sensitive application data is placed in AutoGen's working directory
IF ChatGPT Desktop is granted access to uploaded files or supported macOS app files
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of shared working directories
Restrict ChatGPT Desktop to non-sensitive test data
Run AutoGen in a Docker executor with isolated storage
Turn off app-context access unless needed
requires-engineering: enforce DLP or redaction before either agent sees files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; ChatGPT Desktop can read files and clipboard content but cannot write files. There is no direct write-write conflict, but AutoGen can mutate shared artifacts that ChatGPT then consumes, creating contention on the same workspace. Because the shared-state model is developer-defined and not locked by default, the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or project tree
IF AutoGen writes artifacts that ChatGPT Desktop later reads
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Make AutoGen outputs read-only before ChatGPT consumes them
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo
Use a lock file for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a code-executing orchestration framework, and ChatGPT Desktop can read files and app context. If ChatGPT treats AutoGen-produced text, code, or summaries as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect actions or copied code without verification. The pair has no documented verification gate, so the default pathway is dangerous enough for high severity.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop uses AutoGen output as the basis for code, summaries, or actions
IF no human or automated verification step checks AutoGen output before reuse
mitigations: Require a human review step before reuse
Ask ChatGPT to cite source files for every claim
Separate drafting from execution roles
Mark AutoGen outputs as untrusted in prompts
requires-engineering: add automated validation of generated artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen can handle model-provider API keys and broad filesystem data, while ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code. If regulated or residency-bound data is routed through both, retention and jurisdictional obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so medium is warranted rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data such as customer files or screenshots is processed by both agents
IF the operator relies on one agent's retention or deletion behavior for the other
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows
Use separate accounts for sensitive and non-sensitive work
Document retention expectations for each agent
Delete temporary files after each session
requires-engineering: perform a formal residency and retention review
